proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: the orbit t(s^{-1}({u})) is finite since s has finite fibres; cutting Z = R \ s^{-1}(W) cap t^{-1}(W) out of R, its image t(Z) is closed (t is finite, hence closed), so W' = U \ t(Z) is an R-invariant open inside W containing the orbit; an algebra lemma gives f with the orbit inside D(f) subset W'; the norm g = Norm_s(t-sharp f) is nonzero at u and D(g) consists exactly of the points w whose whole R-equivalence class has f nonzero, so D(g) is an R-invariant affine open containing u (source lines 5152-5192)
